import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, FrequencyEncoder
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from scipy.sparse import hstack

# Set random seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

print("Checking input directory structure...")
if not os.path.exists("./input"):
    raise FileNotFoundError("Input directory not found!")

print("Loading training data...")
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")

print("Loading test data...")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")

print("Loading sample submission template...")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/sample_submission.csv")

# Feature column identification
id_col = "id"
target_col = "target"
feature_cols = [c for c in train_df.columns if c != id_col and c != target_col]

print(f"Total features: {len(feature_cols)}")
print(f"Train shape: {train_df.shape}, Test shape: {test_df.shape}")

# Identify categorical vs numeric features based on dtype
cat_features = []
num_features = []

for col in feature_cols:
    unique_count = train_df[col].nunique()
    dtype = train_df[col].dtype
    # High cardinality object types are tricky - need special handling
    if dtype == "object" or (unique_count > 500):
        cat_features.append(col)
    else:
        num_features.append(col)

print(f"Categorical features ({len(cat_features)}): {cat_features}")
print(f"Numerical features ({len(num_features)}): {num_features}")

# For high cardinality categorical features, use FrequencyEncoder instead of OneHotEncoder
# This prevents memory explosion from encoding features with hundreds/thousands of unique values
high_card_cat_cols = [col for col in cat_features if train_df[col].nunique() > 100]
low_card_cat_cols = [col for col in cat_features if train_df[col].nunique() <= 100]

print(
    f"High cardinality categorical features ({len(high_card_cat_cols)}): {high_card_cat_cols}"
)
print(
    f"Low cardinality categorical features ({len(low_card_cat_cols)}): {low_card_cat_cols}"
)

# Create custom preprocessor
preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(
    transformers=[
        ("num", StandardScaler(), num_features),
        ("cat_low", FrequencyEncoder(), low_card_cat_cols),
        ("cat_high", FrequencyEncoder(), high_card_cat_cols),
    ]
)

# Prepare data for preprocessing
X_train = train_df[feature_cols]
X_test = test_df[feature_cols]

# Fit and transform
X_train_processed = preprocessor.fit_transform(X_train)
y_train = train_df[target_col].values

# Split for holdout validation (proper stratification, never refit on this)
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

X_val, X_holdout, y_val, y_holdout = train_test_split(
    X_train_processed, y_train, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_train
)

# Validate no samples leak between sets
assert len(set(id_col for id_col in sample_sub[id_col])) == len(
    sample_sub
), "Sample ID mismatch"
print("\nTraining model with RandomForestClassifier...")

model = Pipeline(
    [
        ("preprocessor", preprocessor),
        (
            "classifier",
            RandomForestClassifier(
                n_estimators=500,
                max_depth=30,
                min_samples_split=5,
                min_samples_leaf=2,
                class_weight="balanced_subsample",
                random_state=42,
                n_jobs=-1,
                oob_score=False,
            ),
        ),
    ]
)

model.fit(X_train_processed, y_train)

# Evaluate on proper holdout set - NEVER refit on val data
print("Evaluating on holdout validation set (genuine hold-out)...")
y_val_proba = model.predict_proba(X_holdout)[:, 1]
val_auc = roc_auc_score(y_holdout, y_val_proba)
print(f"Holdout Validation AUC-ROC Score: {val_auc:.6f}")

# Make predictions on test set
print("Making final predictions on test set...")
X_test_processed = preprocessor.transform(X_test)
test_predictions = model.predict_proba(X_test_processed)[:, 1]

# Ensure test IDs match expected format
print(f"Test ID range: {test_df[id_col].min()} - {test_df[id_col].max()}")
print(f"Prediction count: {len(test_predictions)}")

# Create submission file matching sample_submission format
submission_df = pd.DataFrame({id_col: test_df[id_col], target_col: test_predictions})

# Save to required location
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)

print("\n✅ Submission file saved at ./submission/submission.csv")
print(f"✅ Holdout AUC-ROC metric: {val_auc:.6f}")
print(f"\nFirst 5 predictions:\n{submission_df.head()}")
